title: Two mothers (1 Kings 3:16–28)
hookLine: a sword, a baby, and the real mother gives him up to save him

cards: Two women stand before the king, and only one of them is telling the truth. They share a house, and each has given birth, a few days apart. One night one of the babies died, and now both claim the living one.
The text is careful to say there was no stranger in the house. No witnesses. One says: she swapped them while I slept.
The other says: no, the living one is mine. This is the young king who just asked for an understanding heart, and here is a case with no way in. Just two voices and one child.

teach.b: The king says one short line: "Bring me a sword." Then the order: divide the living child in two, half to each. It sounds monstrous.
There are no facts to find, so Solomon builds a moment where the answer has to show itself.

teach.h: HER BOWELS YEARNED UPON HER SON.
teach.b: The real mother speaks, in the King James words, "for her bowels yearned upon her son." That's older English for something deep in the body: everything inside her turned toward him.
"O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it."
She loses on purpose, to keep him breathing. The other woman says, "Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it." She wants nobody to have him.
Then the king repeats the first mother's own words back, and adds one line: "Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof."
The proof that she's his mother is that she was willing to stop being called his mother.
Some readers hear the story mainly as a portrait of Solomon, and the chapter ends that way: all Israel saw "that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment."
Other readers notice the real wisdom in the room might belong to the woman whose name we never learn, who knew that winning and loving had come apart, and chose the child.
Either way, it's yesterday's request at work: a heart that hears the difference between someone who wants to be right and someone who wants the child to live.

how: Some Christians read the judgment of Solomon as the wisdom he asked for in 1 Kings 3 put into practice, and some preachers dwell on the true mother as a picture of self-giving love.

games.q: you're the real mother. the king has called for a sword and ordered the living child cut in two. what do you say?
o: insist he's mine until the king believes me.
give her the living child, and in no wise slay it.
say nothing and trust the king to see the truth.
games.why: she gives up her claim to save his life, and that is exactly how the king knows: "she is the mother thereof."

practice: Let one ongoing argument come to mind, and ask what it would cost to stop needing to win it: not to agree or pretend, just to set the winning down for the person's sake.
Picture the two of you a year from now and ask which matters more then, the point or the person. If you pray, hold that person before God.

wordCard.voice: Two mothers. One wanted to win, one wanted the child alive, and the king told them apart by what each was willing to give up.

orig.note: Hebrew: her compassion, her deep feeling, in 1 Kings 3:26, where the King James says her bowels yearned.

carryVoice: Your line: the real mother. She lost the case and kept the child. That's day seven hundred twenty-seven.
